purpose: One pinned starry boundary: starry (Luger et al. 2019) owns spherical-harmonic brightness maps, their intensities and the star-planet light curves they make, as published fits made with it parameterise them. cssEarth owns the paper transcription, the conversion to brightness temperature and scientific qualification.
license: starry is copyright 2019-2021 Rodrigo Luger under the MIT license (STARRY-LICENSE.txt, from its 1.2.0 wheel). Theano-PyMC is BSD-3-Clause, PyMC3 Apache-2.0, exoplanet MIT; NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib and Astropy are BSD-style.
platform: The lock pins the files pip resolves on macOS arm64 with Python 3.9; another platform needs its own hashes added to the lock.
why: starry 1.2.0 is the last release on the Theano backend that published fits used. It needs Theano-PyMC 1.1.2 and PyMC3 3.11.5, which need NumPy below 1.22, so it has its own environment rather than the astroquery toolchain's Python 3.12 and NumPy 2.
compilerFlag: PyMC3 3.11.5 adds -fno-exceptions to Theano's C++ flags on every platform (a workaround for old GCC on Windows); starry's compiled operators throw C++ exceptions, so Apple clang refuses them. The runner removes that one flag from theano.config.gcc__cxxflags after importing starry. No starry code is changed or bypassed. Theano compiles into the toolchain directory and HOME is an empty directory there.
